subject: Post-demo: EverChat hosted API burn sensitivity & throttling windows
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@everchat.com>
Cc: Alec Turner <alec@everchat.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: EverChat hosted API burn sensitivity & throttling windows

Thanks Priya — great to meet the EverChat team today. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can get a pricing scenario together.

Summary (what we heard):
- Primary use: in-chat assistant for customer support (mixed assistant + extraction). Traffic shape: steady baseline with daily spikes tied to marketing campaigns.
- Ballpark monthly tokens today: you said "~50M" with potential growth to ~150M in 6–9 months depending on adoption.
- Peak window: your largest burst last quarter reached roughly 200 TPS sustained for ~20 minutes; expected marketing-driven peaks could hit ~400 TPS for 1–3 hours.
- Target budget: you called out a target $/1M tokens in the mid-teens but asked for options across $8–$18 depending on SLAs and burst capacity.

Clarifying asks for the pricing model we’ll run:
1) Please confirm the expected steady-state monthly tokens (best estimate for next 3 months): low / mid / high
2) Confirm expected peak TPS during campaign windows (single number or range) and typical window duration
3) Any hard latency SLOs (99th percentile) or model-quality constraints (must use model X vs open variants)

Attached the deck and a lightweight pricing template — fill in the steady/peak numbers and I’ll run Hosted vs Dedicated scenarios with unit-cost math and burst allowances.

Next steps: if you confirm numbers by end of week we’ll send a hosted pricing sensitivity table and a recommended rollout plan (canary + traffic shaping).

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.com

Attachments:
- everchat-demo-deck.pdf (presentation)
- pricing-scenario.csv (blank template)

From: Priya Sharma <priya@everchat.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: EverChat hosted API burn sensitivity & throttling windows

Thanks Michael — nice recap. Quick responses inline.

Steady-state monthly tokens (3-month look): 55,000,000 (likely); optimistic high if adoption accelerates: 140,000,000.
Peak TPS: typically 180–220 TPS for short tests; our largest campaign last month spiked to 420 TPS sustained for ~45 minutes. For planning assume peak 420 TPS and a worst-case 800 TPS transient for <10 minutes.
Latency SLO: 99th <= 400ms is preferred; 99th <= 600ms acceptable for peak campaigns if cost tradeoffs help.
Model constraints: prefer GPT-4-class quality for customer-facing answers but can accept mix (smaller open models) for non-critical extraction paths.

Budget: internal target is roughly $700–$1,500/month initially; we understand this is tied to $/1M tokens and are flexible for commitment-based pricing.

Cc'ing Alec (ops) — he’ll fill in exact campaign windows in the spreadsheet.

— Priya

Can you do a quick Hosted vs Dedicated sketch with these constraints? Key asks:
- Dollar-per-1M scenarios at $8 / $12 / $16 tiers and impact on monthly bill for 55M and 140M
- Recommended runtime knobs: batching, KV prefix caching, and quantized model suggestions to hit 99th <= 400ms on our hosted tier
- Can we offer a burst allowance (short 800 TPS buffer) without committing to Dedicated right away?

If convenient, add a row for a 6-month stepped commit showing blended $/1M under a reserve.

Priya and Alec — we’ll aim to send the sensitivity table by end of day tomorrow.

Michael — quick baseline math and recommendations below. Attached a CSV with three price-tier scenarios.

Baseline math (token units rounded):
- 55M tokens/month:
  - $8 / 1M => $440
  - $12 / 1M => $660
  - $16 / 1M => $880
- 140M tokens/month:
  - $8 => $1,120
  - $12 => $1,680
  - $16 => $2,240

Peak handling:
- For 420 TPS sustained on hosted we recommend:
  - Continuous batching + 200ms batching horizon for short requests
  - Prefix/KV caching for repeated assistant prompts (can cut token execution by ~15–25%)
  - Model suggestion: mix of mid-sized open model for extraction, and a quantized 13B/30B variant for critical answers. Quantized path reduces cost and improves throughput.
- For 800 TPS short bursts:
  - Offer burst credits: allow tumbling buffer of ~15–30 minutes using ephemeral extra capacity (billed at higher unit rate) to avoid dedicated commit.

SLA/latency:
- With the above, expected 99th ~ 350–450ms depending on model. If Priya needs deterministic 99th <= 400ms, recommend a small Dedicated burst pool that holds warm worker fractions during known campaign windows.

Next steps:
1) Michael — send this back to EverChat with the attached pricing-scenario.csv.
2) If they confirm steady/peak windows we can sketch a 3-month canary + a ramp plan and propose a 6-month blended commit.

Attachments:
- pricing-scenario.csv (pricing tiers & math)
